_releases.body:
PocketVina 0.3.0 adds the PocketVina Atlas: a database of docking results of drugs against the whole human proteome,
computed in advance with PocketVina. You can now search these results, look at them in 3D and download them from
Python or the command line, with no GPU and no docking of your own.

    pip install -U pocketvina

Documentation: https://bioinformatics.mdc-berlin.de/PocketVina/atlas.html
Atlas database: https://bimsbstatic.mdc-berlin.de/akalin/asarigun/pocketvina_atlas/

## Changes
- `pocketvina.Atlas`: search proteins and drugs, show their information, list the best scores of a protein or a drug,
  select a protein–drug pair, view it in 3D, run PoseBusters checks, save the poses, and download part of the Atlas
  for offline use
- The `pocketvina atlas` command: `search`, `show`, `export` and `download`
- A new documentation page for the Atlas, with an interactive example
- Examples: `example/atlas.py` and a Colab notebook
  ([open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BIMSBbioinfo/PocketVina/blob/main/notebooks/atlas_colab.ipynb)),
  no GPU needed
- The benchmarks page moved out of the documentation; see
  [benchmark/README.md](https://github.com/BIMSBbioinfo/PocketVina/blob/main/benchmark/README.md)
_releases.name: PocketVina v0.3.0

_releases.body:
PocketVina 0.2.0 adds a new results format, faster runs, and tools to inspect and check the results.

    pip install pocketvina

Documentation: https://bioinformatics.mdc-berlin.de/PocketVina/

## Changes
- Results format: Parquet tables and one compact pose file per protein. A stopped run resumes where it stopped.
- Faster runs: seeded ligand preparation, faster receptor conversion, and several engines sharing one GPU.
- New methods: `best_scores()`, `select()`, `show()` (interactive 3D page), `bust()` (PoseBusters) and `export()`.
- Command line: `pocketvina dock`, `info`, `query`, `export`, `show`, `bust`, `setup` and `bench`.
- Documentation, a Google Colab notebook and a conda recipe.

Results of 0.1 remain usable: `pocketvina import-legacy` converts an old output folder, and `ligand_prep="legacy"`
reproduces the ligand preparation of the published runs.
_releases.name: PocketVina v0.2.0

### Compatibility

- **Portable wheels.** Each Linux wheel supports CPython 3.12, 3.13, and
  3.14 on its CPU architecture, either x86_64 or aarch64. The host needs
  NVIDIA driver 580 or newer and glibc 2.34 or newer. An NGC image and a
  local CUDA Toolkit are no longer required to install or run the wheel.
  Some dependencies need build tools; Triton also needs a C compiler and
  Python headers when it first runs a model.

### Breaking Changes

- **CUDA graph configuration.** `optimize()` accepts graph region roles
  or paths. Former module keys such as `token_transformer` and
  `structure_pairformer` now raise `ValueError`; use the enclosing
  region's role or path instead.

### Performance

- **Protenix sampling.** An optional frame-reuse mode skips some denoiser
  evaluations during a 200-step rollout. It is off by default and is an
  approximation, so enabling it can change predictions.
- **Attention.** Protenix atom attention and pair-biased attention use
  faster paths for supported inputs.
  
See the [full release notes][release-notes].

[release-notes]: https://docs.nvidia.com/bionemo/inference-runtime/release-notes/0.2.1

_releases.body:
### EcoliTyper v1.4.0 Release Notes

This release adds mobile genetic element profiling, disk management controls for large cohorts, and a new browser for public genome selection. It also fixes a few issues that surfaced on large-scale runs.
New Features

## MGE Profiling (mobileOG-db).

 Every genome now gets mobile genetic element profiling through the mobileOG-db database. Twelve columns of per-hit detail are parsed, aggregated per sample, and displayed in a dedicated interactive tab with per-lineage aggregate views.

## Report-Level Disk Management.
 A new --report-level {final,summary,full} flag gives explicit control over intermediate output. On a 1,000-genome cohort, final keeps the run under roughly 80 MB, summary (default) retains batch summaries, and full keeps everything. A safety check prevents pruning when the final report directory is missing or empty.

## ECLIPSE Browser. 

A new browser-based companion at https://bbeckley-hub.github.io/eclipse/ provides access to 431,592 public E. coli genomes. Users can filter by MLST, phylogroup, serotype, CH type, pathotype, AMR genes, virulence factors, country, source, host, and collection year, then export a plain-text accession list for NCBI datasets. No installation, account, or API key required.

## MLST Database Management. 

Two new commands mirror the StaphScope workflow. --pull-mlst-db downloads a pre-built scheme from GitHub in about two minutes with no API key. --update-mlst-db fetches the latest alleles from PubMLST in 10 to 20 minutes and requires a one-time API key.

## Species Gate. 

FASTA QC now writes FASTA_QC_species_passed.txt. Only samples that pass the E. coli / Shigella species check proceed to downstream modules. Non-target assemblies are excluded with a logged warning, avoiding false-positive MLST, serotype, and AMR calls.

## Complete Subprocess Logging.
 ecolityper_run.log now captures full stdout and stderr from every module without truncation. When a module fails, its complete output is echoed to the console with the traceback.
Improvements

## Docker image overhaul. 

The image is now rebuilt on mambaorg/micromamba with a BuildKit cache mount. Compressed size drops from over 5 GB to about 1.8 GB. All databases (AMRFinderPlus, MLST Achtman, ABRicate, mobileOG-db) are baked in during build, so first-run network calls are zero. Code-only rebuilds finish in about 30 seconds.


## Upgrade Notes

Conda users should run ecolityper --pull-mlst-db and ecolityper --update-amr-db once after upgrading. Docker and Singularity users skip this step because every database is already inside the image.

For large cohort runs on shared filesystems, add --report-level final to avoid hitting quota with intermediate files.
Citation

If you use EcoliTyper or ECLIPSE in your research, please cite:

Beckley B, Amarh V. EcoliTyper: a species-optimized computational pipeline for comprehensive genotyping and surveillance of Escherichia coli. BMC Bioinformatics. 2026;27:182. doi:10.1186/s12859-026-06529-6
_releases.name: EcoliTyper v1.4.0

_releases.body:
GenomeSpy for Python 0.9.0 upgrades the bundled renderer and generated grammar to GenomeSpy Core 1.3.0.

### New authoring support

- Figwig lazy data sources, branch and values transforms, category and interactive legend selections, categorical grouping and zooming, dendrogram domain outputs, and rule fills and borders.
- Generated public schema-class exports alongside the existing Python builders. New schema features are discovered by the generator rather than added individually by hand.

### Fixes and compatibility

- Adopt upstream fixes for shared hover, categorical-domain updates and multi-column legends.
- Preserve nested branch transforms and container union annotations in generated APIs.
- Reuse checked schema setup to speed repeated serialization while retaining validation of every instance and changed custom schemas.
- Empty ungrouped aggregates now emit zero-valued rows; selection projection follows the expanded Core grammar.
- Retain v0.8.1's native notebook sizing fixes. Straight-link SVG exports, zero-height dendrogram viewports and exact brush-boundary matching remain known upstream limitations. Additional Scanpy integration workflows using the new capabilities remain separate work.

```sh
pip install --upgrade genome-spy-python
```

[Documentation](https://genomespy.app/genome-spy-python/) · [Full changelog](https://github.com/genome-spy/genome-spy-python/compare/v0.8.1...v0.9.0)
_releases.name: GenomeSpy for Python 0.9.0

_releases.body:
### Fixed

- Make the clustered heatmap gallery example render fully in notebooks through its own matrix and tree dimensions. GenomeSpy computes room for titles, labels, and legends, and the gallery accommodates wrapped guides at narrower widths.
- Document native notebook sizing: fixed and step-sized plots keep their authored dimensions; flexible plots use the space supplied by their container. No global notebook width or height is imposed.

### Using the fix

Use the revised [clustered heatmap example](https://genomespy.app/genome-spy-python/gallery/clustered_heatmap.html). Existing notebooks copied from the previous example should copy the updated chart specification; upgrading the package alone does not rewrite notebook code.

```sh
pip install --upgrade genome-spy-python
```

[Notebook sizing guide](https://genomespy.app/genome-spy-python/user-guide/notebooks.html) · [Before-and-after recordings](https://github.com/genome-spy/genome-spy-python/pull/23#issuecomment-6600080270) · [Full changelog](https://github.com/genome-spy/genome-spy-python/compare/v0.8.0...v0.8.1)

_releases.body:
### 🚀 Features

* `pt.md.Cytokine` provides the cytokine response signatures of the Human Cytokine Dictionary for 90 cytokines in 24 PBMC cell types, as gene sets that the `Enrichment` tests take as `targets` ([#1186](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1186)) @Jenniliu12, @Zethson
* `Statsmodels` fits linear mixed models when the design contains a random intercept such as `~condition + (1 | donor)`, by REML with Satterthwaite t-tests like `lmerTest`, so single cells can be tested while accounting for the samples they come from; the kernel is shared with Dialogue and the `(1 | variable)` syntax with Milo ([#1147](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1147)) @Sizerta, @Zethson
* `assign_mixture_model` also writes the binary cell-by-guide assignment to `adata.layers[output_layer]`, since the per-cell string in `.obs` caps and joins the assigned guides ([#1173](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1173)) @Zethson

### ⚡ Performance

* Augur scores each cross-validation fold in one pass over the forest instead of six scorer passes, skips scikit-learn's per-tree parameter validation and no longer ships the fitted trees back from the workers, with identical metrics and importances on seeded runs ([#1178](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1178)) @Zethson
* Dialogue runs the PMD iterations in a numba kernel (20x per fit) and solves the iterative NNLS on the normal equations, replacing the `sparsecca` dependency; whole runs take 3 to 13 s on 5k to 27k cells, about 2x faster than before with up to half the peak memory, where R needs 2 to 16 minutes ([#1177](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1177)) @Zethson
* `assign_mixture_model` fits each guide on its distinct count values, 20x faster on Papalexi (2.9 s to 0.14 s) and with a third of the peak memory at 100k cells x 500 guides ([#1172](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1172)) @Zethson

### ⚠️ Changed results

* Dialogue reproduces the R reference end to end: REML mixed models with Satterthwaite t-tests like `lmerTest`, R's PMD penalty, permutation test and cell-type pruning, Pearson pre-selection of signature genes, one-sided gene p-values, and `test_phenotype_association` now follows `DIALOGUE.pheno` (first level or `True` as the indicator, pooled `All` row, no Fisher combination) ([#1177](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1177)) @Zethson
* Dialogue orders the shared samples like R's ICU collation, since that order decides the signs of the PMD initialization and with them the programs found ([#1177](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1177)) @Zethson
* Augur is reproducible by default: unseeded estimators and folds are seeded by the subsample index like R Augur, and `predict_differential_prioritization` draws its permuted means without replacement from a seeded generator, as R does ([#1178](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1178)) @Zethson
* Dialogue's `min_cells_per_sample` defaults to R's 15 and only gates the ANOVA feature filter, which now raises below five retained features instead of keeping all of them; `n_permutations` counts the observed fit, so values below 11 cannot pass the default `empirical_alpha` ([#1177](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1177)) @Zethson
* `assign_mixture_model` fits the Poisson-Gaussian mixture by multi-start EM instead of 500 Adam steps from one start, which left thresholds unconverged, swapped the components on high-MOI guides and dropped small guides; thresholds now match crispat run to convergence on 105 of 106 Papalexi guides, `learning_rate` is deprecated and `n_iter` caps the EM iterations ([#1172](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1172)) @Zethson

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

* Augur encodes the condition labels after filtering to two conditions, so binary precision, recall and F1 are no longer NaN when the kept labels were not the first two; those metrics now take the first condition as the positive class like R Augur, `min_cells` defaults to `subsample_size` and applies per condition like R, data sets with fewer than 1000 features skip feature selection like R, per-cell `augur_score` is assigned by exact cell type match, and regressors use unstratified folds ([#1178](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1178)) @Zethson
* Dialogue treated signed log10 p-value z-scores as normal z-scores in phase 3, which inflated strong genes, lost the up/down direction and dropped underflowing genes from the Fisher combination ([#1177](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1177)) @Zethson
* Mixscape's `plot_barplot` no longer fails when the number of target genes is not a multiple of five, and Mixscape takes the control, perturbed and non-perturbed class labels from `control`, `perturbation_type` and the new `non_perturbed_label` instead of hardcoding `NT`, `KO` and `NP`; `plot_heatmap` and `plot_perturbscore` use the `mixscape_class` and `pert_key` columns they are given, `plot_perturbscore` keeps a custom `palette` with `before_mixscape=True`, and `plot_barplot` takes a `palette` ([#1191](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1191)) @kkkklck, @Zethson
* Mixscape takes the minimum number of cells left in a perturbed class from the new `min_cells` instead of `min_de_genes`, as Seurat does, which changes results only for a non-default `min_de_genes` ([#1189](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1189)) @kkkklck, @Zethson
* Milo's `plot_nhood_counts_by_cond` raised with pandas 3.1, which kept the sample column's name on the per-sample index ([#1181](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1181)) @Zethson
* Guide assignment: `assign_by_threshold` and `assign_to_max_guide` accept CSC and sparse-array input, explicitly stored zeros no longer enter the mixture fit, `plot_heatmap` saves a reusable cell order and `only_return_results=True` no longer writes to `adata.var` ([#1172](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1172)) @Zethson

### 🧰 Maintenance

* Require Python 3.13 ([#1172](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1172)) @Zethson
* Build the docs with the shared scverse theme and configuration from `scverse-doc`, with the logo blue as its accent for links and highlights ([#1179](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1179)) @Zethson
* The docs take their accents from the scverse-doc registry and colour the sidebar captions in the logo red ([#1182](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1182)) @Zethson
* Group the docs sidebar into Getting started, Guides, Reference and Project like the other scverse core packages, with a new quickstart that replaces the background page and a new glossary ([#1180](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1180)) @Zethson
* Skip the network tests when a download fails with a `URLError` ([#1184](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1184)) @Zethson
* Keep R from loading the system libpython in the tutorial notebooks on Ubuntu 26.04 ([#1185](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1185)) @Zethson
* Skip PyQt6's stubs in mypy, whose invalid syntax made mypy abort ([#1190](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1190)) @Zethson
* Require LLM usage disclosure in the pull request template ([#1165](https://github.com/scverse/pertpy/pull/1165)) @Zethson

_releases.body:
# Lobster AI 1.2.2

## H5AD saves
- If saving fails before the new H5AD file replaces the previous file, the previous file is kept. A failed first save does not leave a file at the requested destination.
- If the new file has already replaced the previous file and a later step that records the save fails, the new file is kept. The error says that the data was saved and bookkeeping failed, and names the saved path.
- Names that would become the same H5AD key or column name now stop the save with a collision message, rather than keeping only one entry. This includes DE result keys that differ only by `/` versus `__`.
- Existing file permission bits are retained; a new file uses the normal creation permissions. A read-only existing file is refused before anything is written. Saving through a symbolic link updates its resolved target and preserves the link.

- Repeated saves no longer write AnnData's virtual `None` layer alias as an extra `"None"` layer. The fix removes only the alias that is the same object as `X`; it preserves genuine layer data and still refuses key collisions.

These changes apply to the local H5AD backend. They do not make every file writer transactional or provide crash durability. An interrupted save can leave a temporary file. Other hard links to the old file keep the old content. The writer does not copy the old file's ACLs, extended attributes, owner or group to the new file.

## Local setup credentials
- Configure the Python local gateway provider with an API key: `lobster init --non-interactive --omics-os-key <key>`, or `lobster init --non-interactive --use-omics-os` with a usable saved key or `OMICS_OS_API_KEY`. For environment-only configuration, set `LOBSTER_LLM_PROVIDER=omics-os` and `OMICS_OS_API_KEY` without running init.
- `lobster cloud login --api-key <key>` is the supported Python API-key login path. The Python init wizard accepts a key; it does not launch a browser login.
- For managed Cloud sessions, install the npm client with `npm i -g @omicsos/lobster` and use `lobster-cli cloud login --device`. Configure Python separately; do not assume that npm login configures the Python provider.
- On POSIX systems, init creates secret `.env` and global `credentials.env` files at mode `0600` and tightens existing rewrites before writing data. Provider OAuth token files use the same private-write preparation. Secret workspace `.env` backups are created privately before copying their contents; nonsecret provider JSON keeps its separate mode policy.
- If you set up a workspace before 1.2.2, run `lobster init` once or `chmod 600 .env`. Init can tighten an owned regular legacy secret file without changing its contents; a failed mode-only repair prints a warning and a manual command. Use `lobster init --global` for an existing global setup.
- These permission changes are not a Windows ACL guarantee or a guarantee that every file writer is transactional. A required credential creation or permission-setting failure stops setup; partial configuration may remain.

## AI-assistant skills
- The usage guide now distinguishes conversation history from saved analysis data. Its coding-agent examples keep dependent steps in one non-interactive query with explicit supported save options, or load saved inputs in each new query. They no longer assume that reusing a session ID carries unsaved data between processes.
- The guide distinguishes memory-only QC outputs from the files that individual tools save, and explains how to inspect save errors and reload saved H5ADs by file stem.
- Managed Cloud session examples use the npm `lobster-cli` alias and device login. The CLI reference also identifies `lobster command "read <file>"` as a supported command.
- The developer skill manifest includes the CLI and AQUADIF migration references, with coverage tests for the declared files.

## Known limitations
### Omics-OS Cloud access
- Init saves configuration, not an account-access check. It reports that the API key is saved but not checked; do not interpret successful init or local status as verified access. An integrated setup-time account check is planned for a later release.
- Some Cloud requests can disconnect before a response arrives. This is under investigation.

### Legacy saved files
- Earlier H5AD files may contain an extra real `"None"` layer copied from `X`. Existing layers are preserved rather than automatically deleted by the repeated-save fix. Handling that legacy duplication is planned for a later release.
- Runtime credential loading does not repair permissions on legacy secret files or old backups. Run init or use the reported manual command for an eligible setup file; a broader legacy-file migration is planned for a later release.

### Data import
- Some GEO series with supplementary count tables may not be detected automatically; a later release improves this.
- The GEO download does not yet pick the expression matrix of series that ship only a gene-by-cell text file, for example GSE109564. This is planned for a later release. The workaround checked with 1.2.1 is to read the downloaded file with pandas (`pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", index_col=0)`, which gives genes × cells), build an AnnData with cells as observations (`anndata.AnnData(X=scipy.sparse.csr_matrix(df.T.values.astype("float32")), obs=pd.DataFrame(index=df.columns), var=pd.DataFrame(index=df.index))`), write it with `write_h5ad`, and load the `.h5ad` file in Lobster. That historical file-loading check used GSE109564 with 4,487 cells × 20,477 genes; it is not a new acceptance run for this release.
- Some compressed GEO text matrices, for example the GSE109564 matrix, are refused when a few row labels are not recognized as gene names (such as `HGNC:12345`, `Y_RNA` or `Metazoa_SRP`), even if the other labels are. Setting `transpose` explicitly does not change this. Loading these files is planned for a later release.
- If saving a required GEO import fails (for example, disk full), that queue entry cannot be retried in the same session, and a partial file may remain in the workspace. Remove the partial file from the workspace and start a new session.

### Metadata validation
- After metadata has been fetched and cached, `validate_dataset_metadata` can return "Already Validated" without running the metadata validation service. This cached-status reply does not confirm that the requested validation checks ran. This is planned for a later release.

### Differential expression results
- A DE result key with `/` in a comparison group label, which does not collide with another key, can still become unavailable through its saved result pointer after H5AD save and reload. The new collision check does not fix that pointer. Use group labels without `/` before running DE; renaming a dataset or export file afterwards does not repair results that already exist, so rerun them from the original input with `/`-free labels. This is planned for a later release.
- In cluster-versus-rest marker summaries, a "Top 10 Downregulated" heading can appear above genes with a positive fold change. The reported statistics are not affected. This is planned for a later release.

### Notebook export
- After you resume a saved session, a pipeline exported with `/pipeline export` can contain some steps twice, so the exported notebook may repeat filtering or normalization. Check the notebook before you run it again. This is planned for a later release.

### Bulk differential expression
- The direct bulk DE tool (`run_bulk_de_direct`) applies an out-group expression filter by default, which is designed for marker genes. On typical bulk data it can remove most genes; if it removes all of them, the tool refuses and says so. For bulk designs, use `run_de_with_formula`. The default will be revised in a later release.

### Custom code
- Custom code (`execute_custom_code`) runs locally with your own user permissions. Enable it only for agents you trust with your workspace.
- The value your code returns as its result may be at most 16 MiB. If it is larger, Lobster reports that the result could not be read and saves no figure from that run. For large outputs, write them to a file in your workspace or store them as a dataset, and return a short summary instead.

### Figures
- Creating the same HTML view twice at the same moment can leave a duplicate view.
- If Lobster cannot remove an old figure revision's file from disk, the file stays in place and keeps using disk space.
- Local figure deletion is not yet available as a CLI command or agent tool.
- The classic terminal plot dashboard does not list figures saved by custom code; the native figure listing does.
